def bridge_ok(evA,slotA,evB,slotB):
    PA,MA=evA[1][slotA]
    PB,MB=evB[1][slotB]
    return ((MA==0 or (MA&PB)!=0) and
            (MB==0 or (MB&PA)!=0))

lemma: For the current finite compositor implementation, whether a proposed bridge between exposed slots a,b is admissible is a function only of the two exposed P/M pairs B(x)[a], B(z)[b]. Equal boundary records therefore have identical bridge-admissibility behavior at every corresponding exposed slot.
mask_domain: P,M are 6-generator bitmasks; exhaustive domain 0..63 used for each of P_A,M_A,P_B,M_B
scope: Code-level theorem for current implementation. It does not prove that P/M is the uniquely forced abstract admissibility law, nor that a particular T_X contains every field needed by future output/selection. Those are separate algebra-level/output-sufficiency obligations.
